domain_label: Learner Model & Adaptivity — Challenge Calibration (desirable difficulties, ~85% target, interleaving, no-burnout)
purpose: A method for a single-user adaptive study system to keep practice hard enough to build durable learning but not so hard it burns the learner out: it grounds the difficulty target in Bjork's desirable difficulties and the Wilson et al. 2019 ~85% optimal-difficulty result (tagged exactly as the research verified it), uses a per-concept/per-item Elo rating to select the next item near that success band, separates the acquisition-difficulty dial from the FSRS review-retention dial, applies the interleaving-vs-blocking evidence, weights MCQ 'correct' below free recall for the guessing floor, detects when material is easy to shed repetition load, and closes the loop nightly with a burnout-guarded success-band controller.
assumptions: no observed dataset for this learner is supplied; every score here is a heuristic prior, and every empirical claim carries the research file's FACT/ESTIMATE/UNKNOWN tag rather than being asserted as a local measurement
the system is single-user, so population-scale estimators (Deep Knowledge Tracing) are out of scope and Elo is the practical streaming estimator with IRT as the conceptual frame

a separate FSRS memory model already schedules per-card review (its desired_retention dial is owner-tunable 0.8-0.97); this KB governs the acquisition-difficulty dial and defers all per-card scheduling to that model

the ~85% figure is a result about gradient-descent learning algorithms on binary classification (Wilson et al. 2019, optimal error 15.87%) [FACT], applied to human NEW-material practice only as a principled default target [ESTIMATE, high confidence], never as a measured human law
concept-tags, a prerequisite/concept graph, a revlog with per-review durations, and AI-graded free/spoken answers exist as inputs from the sibling learner-model and FSRS KBs
exclusions: the FSRS DSR memory-model formulas, revlog schema and per-card scheduling mechanics (they belong to the spaced-repetition/Anki KB; referenced, not redefined here)

the full weakness-diagnosis error taxonomy (slip/misconception/missing-prerequisite/decay) and its differential-diagnosis probes (they belong to the weakness-modeling KB; this KB only consumes the confusion matrix and the real-vs-under-sampled uncertainty test)

the BKT/DKT/Glicko update-equation derivations and the exact Glicko RD math (the canonical Glicko spec was egress-blocked in research and is [UNKNOWN]; this KB uses an RD-style uncertainty idea, not hard-coded Glicko equations)
question-format authoring and the flashcard-quality rewrite queue (referenced as the consumer of card-difficulty outliers, not designed here)
gamification day-completion UI and the broader nightly pipeline's ingest/re-fit/reporting steps beyond the challenge-calibration step

competency_questions.question: What are desirable difficulties, and why is in-session fluency a misleading signal the system must not optimize for?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: DESIRABLE_DIFFICULTIES names Bjork's four (spacing, interleaving, retrieval practice, generation) as [FACT], and FLUENCY_ILLUSION states that ease during study is a misleading cue so learning is judged by delayed retrieval, not session smoothness

competency_questions.question: What is the ~85% optimal-difficulty result, exactly how is it tagged, and how far does it transfer to human acquisition?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: EIGHTY_FIVE_PCT_RULE states the Wilson et al. 2019 Nature Communications result (optimal error 15.87% for gradient-descent binary classification) as [FACT] and the ~85%-on-new-material human target as [ESTIMATE, high confidence], never a human law

competency_questions.question: Why must the acquisition-difficulty target and the FSRS review-retention target be kept as separate dials?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: ACQUISITION_VS_RETENTION_DIALS separates acquisition difficulty (~80-85% correct on new material) from FSRS desired_retention (0.8-0.97 for review), and RETENTION_CALIBRATION measures the review dial via predicted-R vs actual

competency_questions.question: Why is Elo the practical challenge estimator for a single user rather than DKT or full IRT?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SINGLE_USER_SCOPE marks DKT population-scale/not-applicable and IRT calibration many-respondent, and ELO_CHALLENGE_MATCH uses the Rasch/1PL expectation p=1/(1+e^-(theta-d)) with O(1) updates as the streaming estimator

competency_questions.question: How does the Elo model select the next item so predicted correctness lands near the target band?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: ELO_CHALLENGE_MATCH selects items whose difficulty d gives p(theta,d) approx 0.85 for acquisition drills, and NEW_MATERIAL_QUOTA reserves that quota separate from due reviews

competency_questions.question: Why is a 'correct' on a 4-option MCQ weaker mastery evidence than free recall, and how does the guessing floor enter the calibration?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: GUESSING_FLOOR_WEIGHTING states the IRT 3PL pseudo-guessing c (approx 0.25 for a 4-option MCQ) means an MCQ correct is ~25% chance so its update is down-weighted vs free recall, and GENERATION_RETRIEVAL prefers typed/spoken recall as a desirable difficulty

competency_questions.question: How does the system decide a weakness is real rather than under-sampled before it changes the difficulty?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: UNCERTAINTY_RD uses a Glicko-style rating-deviation idea (RD grows with inactivity, shrinks with answers) so only low-uncertainty concepts drive action, and CONFUSION_DRIVEN_INTERLEAVE consumes that confidence

competency_questions.question: What is the interleaving evidence, and where is blocking still the right call?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: INTERLEAVING_EVIDENCE cites Brunmair & Richter 2019 (g=0.42) and Rohrer et al. 2020 (61% vs 38%, d=0.83) as [FACT] with the math caveat, and BLOCKING_FIRST_EXPOSURE allows blocking only for the very first encounter with a topic

competency_questions.question: How does the confusion matrix decide which concept pairs to interleave?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: CONFUSION_DRIVEN_INTERLEAVE feeds high off-diagonal concept-pairs into the interleaving policy (interleaving trains discrimination), placing confused pairs adjacent-but-not-identical

competency_questions.question: How does the success-band controller loosen or tighten the target, and how is burnout prevented?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SUCCESS_BAND_CONTROLLER loosens toward 0.7 when coasting (rolling 2-week success > 92%) and tightens toward 0.9 when frustrated (success < 70% or abandonment), and BURNOUT_GUARD caps challenge on frustration/abandonment signals

competency_questions.question: How is 'easy for the user' detected and converted into lower repetition load?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: COASTING_DETECTION reads FSRS low-D/high-S plus Elo theta >> d and a rating-honesty check, and LOAD_BUDGETING postpones mastered-easy items first (lowest predicted-R loss) to fit the time budget without touching weak concepts

competency_questions.question: How does the nightly job recalibrate the target and build tomorrow's queue, and what makes a calibration a go?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: NIGHTLY_CALIBRATION_STEP adjusts the band from rolling actuals idempotently, QUEUE_ASSEMBLY orders due reviews + probes + acquisition-quota by interleaving trimmed to budget, CHALLENGE_FEEDBACK_LOOP scores success-vs-band, and CALIBRATION_GO_NOGO passes only when the dials are separate, evidence is guessing-floor-weighted, interleaving is on and burnout is guarded

glossary.definition: Bjork's (1994) term for a condition of practice that feels harder and slows apparent progress but improves long-term retention and transfer; the canonical four are spacing, interleaving, retrieval practice (testing effect) and generation [FACT — Bjork & Bjork 2011].

The misleading cue that smooth, easy in-session performance signals durable learning; because desirable difficulties depress in-session fluency, the system judges learning by delayed retrieval success, not by how easy a session felt [ESTIMATE, high confidence — direct implication of the desirable-difficulties result].

Wilson, Shenhav, Straccia & Cohen, Nature Communications 10:4646 (2019): for a broad class of gradient-descent learners on binary classification, learning rate is maximized at ~85% training accuracy, optimal error 15.87% = Phi(-1) [FACT]. Applied here only as a principled default target of ~80-85% correct on NEW-material practice [ESTIMATE, high confidence], not a measured human law.

Two separate difficulty knobs the system must not conflate: the acquisition-difficulty target (~80-85% correct on new material, from the ~85% rule) and the FSRS review-retention target (desired_retention, owner-tunable 0.8-0.97) [FACT for the FSRS dial].

Each answer is a match between learner ability theta (per concept) and item difficulty d; expected correctness p=1/(1+e^-(theta-d)) with O(1) updates theta <- theta + K(y-p), d <- d - K(y-p) [FACT — Pelanek 2016]; it is an online approximation of Rasch/1PL and picks the next item so p approx 0.85.

The IRT 3PL pseudo-guessing lower asymptote; for a 4-option MCQ random guessing gives c approx 0.25 [FACT], so a 'correct' on such an MCQ carries ~25% chance mass and is weaker mastery evidence than a typed/spoken free-recall correct, and its rating update is down-weighted accordingly.

Glicko's (Glickman 1995) explicit uncertainty around a rating: RD grows during inactivity and shrinks with play [FACT]; used here as an RD-style per-concept uncertainty to decide whether a weakness is real or merely under-sampled before acting. The exact Glicko update equations are [UNKNOWN] (canonical spec was egress-blocked) and are not hard-coded.

Interleaving mixes concept-tags within a session (a desirable difficulty that trains discrimination); Brunmair & Richter 2019 meta-analysis g=0.42, Rohrer et al. 2020 RCT 61% vs 38% delayed, d=0.83 [FACT], with math effects smaller/mixed. Blocking (one tag in a long run) is reserved for the very first encounter with a topic.

The loop that moves the acquisition target inside a band: loosen toward 0.7 when the learner is coasting (rolling 2-week success > 92%), tighten toward 0.9 when frustrated (success < 70% or session abandonment) [ESTIMATE — synthesis of the ~85% mechanism].

The state where material no longer needs much repetition: FSRS low difficulty D + high stability S plus Elo theta well above item d; detected nightly so the specialist stops generating fresh drills and load is budgeted down, guarded by a rating-honesty check (Easy marked but long latency or later lapses).

nodes.definition: Establish the theoretical spine of challenge calibration: Bjork's (1994) desirable difficulties — conditions of practice that feel harder and slow apparent progress yet enhance long-term retention and transfer. The canonical four are spacing, interleaving, retrieval practice (the testing effect) and generation [FACT — Bjork & Bjork 2011, bjorklab.psych.ucla.edu]. The operational consequence for an adaptive system is that difficulty is a feature to engineer, not a defect to remove: the scheduler deliberately introduces spacing, mixes tags, forces recall over re-reading, and prefers generation, accepting lower in-session ease for higher delayed retrieval. Every downstream calibration mechanism in this KB exists to dose these difficulties to the right level rather than to zero.

included: the four canonical desirable difficulties as a FACT
the difficulty-is-a-feature principle
the mandate to dose rather than remove difficulty
excluded: the FSRS spacing mechanics (spaced-repetition KB)
the exact success-rate target (its own node)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a revised synthesis of desirable difficulties or a learner-population constraint changes what difficulty is desirable

pros.claim: Grounding calibration in desirable difficulties stops the system from optimizing for the wrong thing — easy sessions instead of durable learning
pros.example: forcing retrieval and interleaving even though the learner would rate a re-read session as more pleasant

cons.claim: Desirable difficulties are a qualitative principle, not a dosing rule, so alone they cannot say how hard is too hard
cons.example: adding difficulty until the learner disengages because the principle names no ceiling

failure_modes: treating in-session ease as the optimization target
adding difficulty without any success-rate ceiling and driving disengagement

nodes.definition: Encode the corollary the whole controller depends on: fluency during study is a misleading signal of learning [ESTIMATE, high confidence — direct implication of desirable difficulties]. Because desirable difficulties depress in-session ease, a smooth session and a confident self-rating do not imply durable memory; conversely a hard, error-strewn session can be the one that builds it. The system must therefore never let the learner or the scheduler optimize for in-session smoothness, and must judge learning by delayed retrieval success (next-day and later) rather than same-session performance. This is the reason self-graded 'Easy' is treated as a claim to be checked (see coasting detection), not as ground truth.

included: fluency as a misleading cue
judge learning by delayed retrieval not session smoothness
self-rating treated as a checkable claim
excluded: the FSRS interval mechanics that realize delayed retrieval
the numeric success target

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the rating-honesty check reveals this learner's self-ratings are trustworthy or the delayed-retrieval signal is lost

pros.claim: Refusing to optimize for session smoothness prevents the system from rewarding shallow, quickly-decaying encoding
pros.example: declining to shorten a session just because the learner found it easy, and scheduling a delayed retest instead

cons.claim: Ignoring fluency entirely can miss genuine ease and over-drill mastered material, so fluency is a signal to discount, not delete
cons.example: retesting a truly mastered concept as if the easy rating were meaningless

failure_modes: trusting a confident self-rating as evidence of durable learning
letting the scheduler minimize in-session error rate as its objective
acceptance_tests: the analysis states fluency is misleading, that learning is judged by delayed retrieval, and that self-graded ease is a checkable claim not ground truth
revisit_triggers: the rating-honesty check shows self-ratings are in fact well-calibrated for this learner

nodes.definition: Fix the scope constraint that decides which learner models are usable: this is a single-user system, so population-scale estimators are out. Deep Knowledge Tracing (Piech et al. 2015: AUC 0.85 vs 0.68 for BKT on Khan Academy [FACT]) trains across thousands of students and is uninterpretable — noted as the population-scale option, not built [ESTIMATE, high confidence — Khajah et al. 2016 shows the gap largely closes vs extended BKT]. Full IRT calibration needs many respondents per item and is unavailable for one user; it is kept as the conceptual frame (ability vs item difficulty vs guessing floor). The practical estimator is Elo — an online, streaming approximation of Rasch/1PL with O(1) updates that rates the learner and every item at once. This node is why the calibration machinery downstream is Elo-based, not DKT- or IRT-based.

included: the single-user constraint
DKT as population-scale/not-built and IRT as conceptual-only

excluded: the Elo update formula itself (its own node)

cons.claim: Ruling out DKT/full IRT forgoes their accuracy on rich data, so the choice must be revisited if multi-learner data ever appears

nodes.definition: Set the difficulty target and tag it exactly as the research verified it. Wilson, Shenhav, Straccia & Cohen, 'The Eighty Five Percent Rule for optimal learning,' Nature Communications 10:4646 (2019): for a broad class of gradient-descent-based learning algorithms on binary classification tasks, learning rate is maximized at ~85% training accuracy, with optimal error rate exactly 15.87% (= Phi(-1)); demonstrated for artificial and biologically plausible neural networks [FACT]. Crucially this is a result about learning algorithms, not a direct human RCT, so ~85% success on NEW-material practice is adopted as a principled default target, not a law [ESTIMATE, high confidence — scope reading]. It is strikingly consistent with FSRS's default desired retention 0.90 for review, but the two are different quantities and must stay separate dials. This target is the setpoint every controller in the KB steers toward.

the ~85%-on-new-material human target as an ESTIMATE default
the reminder that it is algorithm-derived not a human law
excluded: the FSRS retention dial (its own node)
the item-selection mechanism that realizes the target

pros.claim: A principled, cited setpoint replaces an arbitrary difficulty guess and anchors the whole controller

cons.claim: The result is about learning algorithms, so treating ~85% as an exact human optimum over-reads it and can misfire per learner

failure_modes: citing ~85% as a proven human law rather than an algorithm-derived default

nodes.definition: Enforce the two-dial separation the ~85% result and FSRS jointly demand. Dial A, acquisition difficulty, governs how hard NEW-material practice should be (~80-85% correct, from the ~85% rule) [ESTIMATE default]. Dial B, review retention, is FSRS's owner-tunable desired_retention (0.8-0.97, default ~0.90) governing when already-learned cards come back [FACT for the FSRS dial]. They measure different quantities — accuracy on training items vs retention of learned cards — and steer different subsystems (item selection vs the FSRS scheduler). Conflating them (e.g. pushing desired_retention to 0.85 to 'match' the acquisition target) would over- or under-schedule reviews. This node is the guard that keeps the two controllers from cross-talking.

included: the acquisition dial (~80-85% correct) vs the FSRS retention dial (0.8-0.97)
why they are different quantities and subsystems
the no-conflation guard
excluded: the FSRS scheduling math itself (spaced-repetition KB)

pros.example: tuning acquisition difficulty for a hard new topic without disturbing the review schedule

cons.claim: Two dials add tuning surface and can drift apart if not periodically reconciled in reporting
cons.example: an acquisition target and a retention target that individually make sense but jointly overload a day

nodes.definition: Build the estimator that turns the ~85% setpoint into an item choice. Treat each answer as a match between learner ability theta (per concept) and item difficulty d; expected correctness p = 1 / (1 + e^-(theta - d)); update after observing y in {0,1}: theta <- theta + K(y - p) and symmetrically d <- d - K(y - p), with K regulating step size (K = 0.4 has been considered appropriate in some educational settings) [FACT — Pelanek 2016; formula per the Elo-for-education literature]. A common refinement is to decay K with attempts, K = a/(1 + b*n), so early answers move ratings more [ESTIMATE, medium-high confidence]. This is exactly the Rasch/1PL curve, so Elo is an online streaming approximation of Rasch estimation, and it rates the learner and every item at once with O(1) updates. To calibrate challenge, invert it: pick the next acquisition item whose d gives p(theta, d) approx 0.85.

included: the Elo expectation and symmetric update
K step-size and the K-decay refinement
inverting p to select an item near the target
excluded: the guessing-floor down-weighting of MCQ (its own node)
the RD-style uncertainty (its own node)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: an RD signal, K re-tuning, or a card-difficulty drift changes the Elo estimate or selection

pros.claim: One O(1) dual update rates the learner and every item together, so the same machinery that finds weak concepts also flags miscalibrated cards
pros.example: an item whose d drifts far above its siblings surfacing as a card-quality flag while theta tracks the concept

cons.claim: Elo is a point estimate with no built-in uncertainty, so early or sparse ratings are noisy and can mis-select difficulty
cons.example: selecting an item at p approx 0.85 off a theta estimated from only two answers

failure_modes: driving item selection off a noisy early theta with no uncertainty guard

nodes.definition: Correct the challenge estimate for question format. The IRT 3PL model P(correct|theta) = c + (1-c)/(1 + e^{-a(theta - b)}) has a pseudo-guessing lower asymptote c; for a 4-option MCQ random guessing gives c approx 0.25 [FACT] (2PL sets c=0; 1PL/Rasch also fixes a common a). So a 'correct' on a 4-option MCQ carries roughly 25% chance mass and is weaker mastery evidence than a typed or spoken free-recall correct. The calibration consequence: down-weight the Elo update (and the success-rate accounting) for MCQ corrects relative to free recall, and read a raw MCQ success rate as inflated above true mastery when steering toward the ~85% band. Guessing floor c is a static per-format constant, not a fitted parameter here.

included: the 3PL guessing floor c approx 0.25 for 4-option MCQ
down-weighting MCQ corrects vs free recall in updates and success accounting
c as a static per-format constant
excluded: full IRT item calibration (out of single-user scope)
the choice of question formats (question-types KB)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a format change or a free-recall-vs-MCQ divergence changes the guessing-floor weighting

cons.claim: A single c approx 0.25 constant ignores that estimated c often differs and that distractor plausibility changes effective guessing
cons.example: a 4-option item with two implausible distractors having an effective guess rate well below 25%

failure_modes: treating an MCQ correct as equal evidence to a free-recall correct

acceptance_tests: the analysis states c approx 0.25 for a 4-option MCQ, down-weights MCQ corrects vs free recall in the update and success accounting, and marks c a static per-format constant
revisit_triggers: a format's option count or distractor quality changes its effective guess rate

nodes.definition: Add the uncertainty guard that decides whether a weakness (or an easy signal) is real or merely under-sampled before the controller acts. Glicko (Glickman 1995) extends Elo with a rating deviation RD — an explicit uncertainty around the rating, so estimates are distributions not points; low-RD players move less per result, and RD grows during inactivity and shrinks with play [FACT]. The exact Glicko update equations are [UNKNOWN] — the canonical spec at glicko.net was egress-blocked in research, so they are not hard-coded; only the RD-style uncertainty idea is used. Operationally: maintain an RD-like uncertainty per concept, decay it upward for concepts untouched > N days, and require low RD before letting a low theta drive a difficulty change or an intervention, so the system probes to reduce RD rather than acting on a noisy estimate.

included: RD as explicit rating uncertainty, growing with inactivity
requiring low RD before acting on a weakness
probing to reduce RD
excluded: the exact Glicko equations ([UNKNOWN], not hard-coded)
the diagnosis of why a real weakness exists (weakness-modeling KB)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the Glicko spec becomes available or the RD-decay rate is re-calibrated

pros.claim: Gating action on RD stops the controller from over-reacting to a weakness that is really just an under-sampled concept
pros.example: declining to remediate a concept with one recent wrong answer and high RD until a probe confirms it

cons.claim: Without the verified Glicko equations the RD update is an approximation, so the confidence threshold is itself a tuned heuristic
cons.example: an RD-decay rate set by hand that lets a stale weakness look more certain than it is

failure_modes: acting on a low theta with high RD (under-sampled) as if it were confirmed
hard-coding unverified Glicko equations instead of the RD-style idea
acceptance_tests: the analysis uses an RD-style per-concept uncertainty that grows with inactivity, requires low RD before acting, and flags the exact Glicko equations as UNKNOWN and not hard-coded
revisit_triggers: the canonical Glicko spec becomes fetchable and the equations can be verified

nodes.definition: Ground the interleaving lever in its evidence. Brunmair & Richter 2019 (Psychological Bulletin) meta-analysis of interleaved learning: overall medium positive effect, Hedges' g = 0.42, with mathematical-task effects smaller and mixed (primary studies range strongly negative to positive) [FACT]. Rohrer, Dedrick, Hartwig & Cheung 2020 (J. Educational Psychology), RCT of 787 seventh-graders across 54 classes: on an unannounced delayed test one month later, interleaved scored 61% vs 38% blocked, d = 0.83 [95% CI 0.68-0.97] [FACT]. Mechanism consensus: interleaving works chiefly where items are confusable (the discriminative-contrast hypothesis) [ESTIMATE, high confidence]. Scheduler rules that follow: never drill one concept-tag in a long block past first exposure, and mix tags daily. The caveat (mixed math results) is why blocking survives for first encounters.

included: Brunmair g=0.42 and Rohrer 61% vs 38%, d=0.83 as FACT
the discriminative-contrast mechanism
the no-long-block / mix-tags-daily rule and the math caveat
excluded: the confusion-matrix pair selection (its own node)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a newer interleaving meta-analysis or domain-specific evidence revises the policy

cons.claim: The math effects are smaller and mixed, so blanket interleaving can hurt in domains or at stages where blocking helps encoding
cons.example: interleaving a brand-new procedure before it is even encoded once and stalling initial learning

failure_modes: interleaving everything including first encounters

acceptance_tests: the analysis cites Brunmair g=0.42 and Rohrer 61% vs 38%/d=0.83 as FACT, states the discriminative-contrast mechanism, and carries the mixed-math caveat
revisit_triggers: a newer meta-analysis revises the interleaving effect size

nodes.definition: Carve out the one place blocking still wins: the very first encounter with a topic (initial encoding). Because the interleaving evidence for mathematical tasks is smaller and mixed and interleaving helps chiefly once items are confusable, drilling a brand-new concept-tag in a short block for its first exposure gives the learner a clean encoding before contrast is introduced [ESTIMATE, high confidence — synthesis of the mixed-math results]. The rule is narrow: block only the first encounter, then switch that tag into the interleaved daily mix and never drill it in a long block again. This prevents both errors — interleaving material that has not been encoded once, and blocking material long past the point interleaving would build discrimination.

included: blocking allowed only for the first encounter
the switch to interleaved mix after initial encoding
the two symmetric errors it prevents
excluded: the interleaving effect sizes (their own node)
the queue ordering that applies the rule (its own node)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: evidence on encoding-window length or first-encounter detection changes the blocking rule

cons.claim: The first-encounter boundary is a judgment call, so mis-detecting 'first encounter' can extend blocking too long

nodes.definition: Turn interleaving from generic tag-mixing into targeted pair practice. Maintain a concept x concept confusion matrix M where M[i][j] counts 'asked about i, answered with j's content' (from misconception-tagged distractors or AI-graded free/spoken answers naming the wrong entity); high off-diagonal pairs are discrimination failures [ESTIMATE — design synthesis; the misconception-distractor data is cited]. Because interleaving works precisely by training discrimination between confusable items, the pairs the learner actually confuses are exactly the pairs to interleave: place confused-pair items adjacent-but-not-identical in the daily queue. The uncertainty guard applies — only act on a confusion signal once its RD-style uncertainty is low enough that the confusion is real, not a one-off. This is the bridge from weakness data to the interleaving policy.

placing confused pairs adjacent-but-not-identical
gating on low RD before acting
excluded: the full weakness diagnosis taxonomy (weakness-modeling KB)

nodes.definition: Operationalize two of the four desirable difficulties — retrieval practice and generation — as a format preference the calibrator honors. Retrieval practice (the testing effect) and generation make the learner produce the answer rather than recognize it, which is harder in-session but stronger for retention [FACT — the two are canonical desirable difficulties, Bjork & Bjork 2011]. Combined with the guessing floor, this means the system prefers typed or spoken free-recall items over 4-option recognition where the concept and format allow, and treats a free-recall correct as stronger mastery evidence than an MCQ correct. Recognition MCQs remain useful for speed, coverage and formats that demand them (e.g. certain exam-style items), but the calibrator weights their evidence and difficulty accordingly.

preferring free recall over recognition where possible
MCQ retained for speed/coverage with weighted evidence
excluded: the authoring of specific question types (question-types KB)

pros.example: asking the learner to type the definition rather than pick it from four options

cons.claim: Free-recall grading depends on AI scoring that can be wrong, so over-preferring it imports grading noise into the calibration
cons.example: an AI mis-grading a correct spoken answer as wrong and depressing theta

revisit_triggers: AI free-recall grading accuracy changes

nodes.definition: Define the closed-loop controller that steers the acquisition target inside a band around ~85%. With Elo in place this is nearly one line: select next acquisition items whose difficulty d satisfies p(theta, d) approx 0.85; then adapt the band from rolling actuals — loosen the target toward 0.7 when the learner is coasting (rolling 2-week success > 92%) and tighten toward 0.9 when frustrated (rolling success < 70% or session abandonment) [ESTIMATE — synthesis of the ~85% mechanism]. The controller reads guessing-floor-adjusted success (MCQ corrects discounted) and only moves on low-RD estimates. It is the central knob the nightly step tunes and the feedback loop scores; burnout guarding and coasting detection sit on either side of it as the safety limits.

pros.claim: A banded controller keeps difficulty near the optimum while adapting to the learner's current state instead of holding one rigid number

nodes.definition: Detect when material has become easy so repetition load can be shed — the owner's 'what's easy doesn't require too much repetition.' This reuses FSRS's own encoding rather than duplicating it [FACT for FSRS fields]: per-card difficulty D in [1,10] and stability S already exist; concepts whose cards have low mean D + high median S, together with Elo theta well above item d, are 'mastered-easy.' A rating-honesty check guards it: if the user marks Easy but response latency is long or later lapses are high, flag over-optimistic self-grading (the revlog stores per-review duration, capped 60s) [FACT, FSRS file] — consistent with the fluency illusion. Detected coasting concepts get longer initial steps and the specialist stops generating fresh drills there; it is the input to load budgeting.

nodes.definition: Impose the safety ceiling that keeps 'keep it challenging' from becoming 'burn the learner out.' Frustration and disengagement signals — rolling success < 70%, session abandonment mid-session, and chronically-unfinished plans — cap how hard the controller may push, overriding the desirable-difficulty pull toward more challenge [ESTIMATE — synthesis; the abandonment/plan-adherence signals are the system's own metrics]. On these signals the guard forces the success band toward 0.9 (easier), protects a floor of wins per session, and prefers postponing new-material load over deepening difficulty. It also reframes a chronically 60%-done plan as a bad plan, not a bad learner, feeding the schedule-adherence loop. The guard is deliberately asymmetric: it can only make the near-term experience easier, never harder.

forcing the band toward 0.9 and protecting a win floor

nodes.definition: Convert coasting detection into an actual reduction in daily repetition load within the owner's time budget. Predicted daily review load is computable from the stability (S) distribution [FACT, FSRS file]; when tomorrow's projected load exceeds the budget, the nightly job trims by postponing mastered-easy cards first — the items with the lowest predicted-recall (R) loss from a short delay — never weak-concept or acquisition cards [ESTIMATE — design synthesis]. This gives the owner's 'what's easy doesn't need much repetition' as an explicit, ordered budget rule: shed load from the strong end, protect the fragile end. It depends on coasting detection to know which cards are safely postponable and hands its trimmed set to queue assembly.

nodes.definition: Measure the review-retention dial so it can be trusted separately from the acquisition dial. For every review the FSRS model gives a predicted recall R at that moment; bin reviews by predicted R (e.g. deciles) and compare to the observed recall rate to build a per-bin calibration table plus a Brier score / log-loss — log-loss being the exact objective the FSRS optimizer trains on [FACT, FSRS file]. A daily calibration snapshot yields trend lines and, when the predicted-vs-actual gap widens after a re-fit, a signal to revert parameters. This node is why the acquisition target and the retention target stay honestly separate: the retention dial is validated against actuals rather than assumed correct.

included: predicted-R vs actual binning, Brier/log-loss, daily snapshot

excluded: the FSRS optimizer internals (spaced-repetition KB)
the acquisition-band control (its own node)

nodes.definition: Reserve and size the acquisition stream that the ~85% target actually applies to. New-material items are selected at p(theta, d) approx 0.85 via Elo (acquisition difficulty), distinct from due FSRS reviews (governed by the retention dial) [ESTIMATE — synthesis; the FSRS review side is FACT]. The quota is a protected daily allotment: load budgeting may postpone mastered-easy reviews but must not raid the acquisition quota to fit the time budget, because new learning is the point. The quota interacts with the guessing floor (an MCQ-heavy acquisition set needs more items to reach equivalent free-recall evidence) and with burnout guarding (the guard may shrink the quota, but shrinking is its only lever on it). This node makes 'keep learning new things at the right difficulty' an explicit, defended budget line.

nodes.definition: Place challenge calibration as an idempotent step in the nightly analysis batch. After the job replays the day's guessing-floor-weighted answers through Elo (theta per concept, d per item) and decays RD upward for untouched concepts, the challenge-calibration step adjusts the target success band from the rolling 2-week actuals per the success-band controller, honoring the burnout guard [ESTIMATE — design synthesis; the pipeline machinery it sits in is grounded in the cited models]. It must be safe to re-run: a crash mid-job and a rerun produce the same band, because the step is a pure function of the stored actuals and prior band, never an in-place mutation of history. This is where the controller's tuning actually happens each day, feeding queue assembly and the feedback loop.

idempotency / safe re-run as a pure function of stored data

nodes.definition: Give challenge calibration its own scorecard in the system's self-metrics, closing the outer loop. The metric is the rolling success rate versus the target band (guessing-floor-adjusted), computed from daily answers, with a stored daily snapshot (trend not point), a threshold, and a named action — move the difficulty dial [ESTIMATE — design synthesis]. Like every self-metric it must have a consumer or be deleted. It sits alongside prediction-calibration, card-quality and schedule-adherence loops but owns exactly the challenge dimension: is the learner actually being held near the optimal difficulty over time, and does the diagnosis-and-fix machinery recover weaknesses within K days. It reads from the nightly step and the burnout guard and reports into the go/no-go verdict.

nodes.definition: Assemble tomorrow's ordered queue — the concrete artifact challenge calibration produces. Combine due FSRS reviews, diagnostic probe items, and the protected new-material acquisition quota, order them by the interleaving rules (mix concept-tags; place confused pairs adjacent-but-not-identical; block only true first encounters), select acquisition items at p approx 0.85, prefer free-recall over recognition where feasible, then trim to the time budget by postponing mastered-easy items first [ESTIMATE — design synthesis; each ingredient is grounded in its cited node]. The ordering is where interleaving, blocking, the guessing floor, the acquisition quota and load budgeting all resolve into a single sequence. It is idempotent and produced by the nightly job; a bad plan that is chronically unfinished feeds back as a plan problem, not a learner problem.

nodes.definition: Compose the merged verdict the whole KB builds toward: a challenge calibration is a go only when every binding gate clears. The verdict intersects four lenses — difficulty setpoint honesty (the ~85% target is applied as an ESTIMATE default, not a human law, and the acquisition and FSRS-retention dials are kept separate), evidence integrity (success is read guessing-floor-adjusted and only on low-RD estimates), difficulty engineering (interleaving is on with confused pairs targeted, blocking only for first encounters, generation/retrieval preferred), and learner protection (the burnout guard caps challenge and the feedback loop tracks success-vs-band) [ESTIMATE — synthesis]. Reconciled rules: never optimize for in-session fluency; never conflate the two dials; never act on a high-RD weakness; never push challenge through burnout signals; never quote ~85% as a proven human law. A calibration that is theoretically sound but fails a gate is a no-go until the gate clears.

conflict_axes.name: desirable_difficulty_vs_burnout
conflict_axes.description: Desirable difficulties push challenge up for long-term retention while learner engagement caps how hard practice can get before disengagement.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: bound challenge inside the success band and let the burnout guard force it easier (toward 0.9) only on frustration/abandonment signals, acting solely in the easier direction

conflict_axes.name: in_session_fluency_vs_delayed_retrieval
conflict_axes.description: In-session ease is pleasant and easy to measure but a misleading signal, whereas delayed retrieval is the true target and costs more to observe.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: never optimize for in-session smoothness; treat self-rated ease as a checkable claim and score learning by next-day and later retrieval

conflict_axes.name: acquisition_target_vs_retention_target
conflict_axes.description: The ~85% acquisition-difficulty target resembles the FSRS ~0.90 retention target but measures a different quantity and steers a different subsystem.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: keep the acquisition dial (~80-85% correct on new material) and the FSRS retention dial (0.8-0.97) separate and validate each against its own actuals

conflict_axes.name: mcq_speed_vs_free_recall_evidence
conflict_axes.description: MCQs are fast and easy to grade but carry a ~25% guessing floor, while free recall is stronger evidence but slower and reliant on AI grading.
poles: favor free recall for evidence strength
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: prefer generation/free recall where feasible and down-weight MCQ corrects by the guessing floor in both updates and success accounting

conflict_axes.name: act_now_vs_confirm_weakness
conflict_axes.description: Acting fast on a low rating is responsive but a low theta may be under-sampled noise, while probing to confirm costs queue slots.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: require low RD before acting on a weakness or easy signal; spend a few probe slots to reduce RD rather than react to a noisy point estimate

conflict_axes.name: interleaving_vs_blocking
conflict_axes.description: Interleaving trains discrimination and wins on delayed tests, but blocking gives cleaner initial encoding, with math effects mixed.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: block only the very first encounter with a topic, then interleave that tag; target confused pairs adjacent-but-not-identical thereafter

conflict_axes.name: shed_load_vs_protect_new_learning
conflict_axes.description: Fitting the time budget wants to trim items while protecting new learning wants to keep the acquisition quota intact.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: postpone mastered-easy reviews first (lowest predicted-R loss) and never raid the acquisition quota; only the burnout guard may shrink it

conflict_axes.name: principled_default_vs_overclaimed_law
conflict_axes.description: The ~85% result is a strong, cited default but is derived from learning algorithms, not a human RCT, so it must not be quoted as a human law.
poles: treat ~85% as a proven human optimum
treat it as a tagged ESTIMATE default
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: apply ~85% as a principled default target tagged ESTIMATE, keep the 15.87% algorithmic result as FACT, and allow per-learner divergence

conflict_axes.name: streaming_simplicity_vs_model_richness
conflict_axes.description: Elo is O(1), interpretable and single-user friendly but a point estimate, whereas DKT/full IRT are richer but need population data.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: use Elo as the practical single-user estimator with an RD-style uncertainty, keeping DKT/full IRT as conceptual/population-scale options not built

edge_cases.description: The ~85% figure is quoted as a proven human optimal-learning law rather than an algorithm-derived, tagged default
edge_cases.trigger: someone cites the Nature Communications result as a human RCT finding
edge_cases.mitigation: keep the 15.87% result FACT and the ~85% human target ESTIMATE, state it is algorithm-derived, and allow per-learner divergence

edge_cases.description: FSRS desired_retention is pushed to 0.85 to 'match' the acquisition target, mis-scheduling reviews
edge_cases.trigger: the acquisition and retention dials are conflated into one number
edge_cases.mitigation: keep the two dials separate; leave FSRS desired_retention on its own 0.8-0.97 scale validated by predicted-R-vs-actual

edge_cases.description: A raw MCQ success rate near 85% is read as on-target while true free-recall mastery is far lower
edge_cases.trigger: success is accounted without discounting the ~25% MCQ guessing floor
edge_cases.mitigation: compute success on guessing-floor-adjusted evidence and weight free-recall corrects above MCQ corrects

edge_cases.description: A concept with one recent wrong answer and high RD is remediated as a confirmed weakness
edge_cases.trigger: the controller acts on a low theta without checking rating deviation
edge_cases.mitigation: require low RD before acting; issue a probe to reduce RD before remediating or changing difficulty

edge_cases.description: A brand-new topic is interleaved on its first exposure and initial encoding stalls
edge_cases.trigger: the interleaving policy is applied before any clean first encounter
edge_cases.mitigation: block only the first encounter for clean encoding, then fold the tag into the interleaved mix

edge_cases.description: The success band oscillates, loosening after one good week and tightening after one bad session
edge_cases.trigger: the band adapts off a rolling window that is too short or thresholds that are too tight
edge_cases.mitigation: use a stable ~2-week rolling window and hysteresis on the >92% / <70% thresholds to damp oscillation

edge_cases.description: The learner speed-clicks Easy, inflating stability while true recall decays and repetition is wrongly shed
edge_cases.trigger: coasting is declared from self-ratings without the latency/later-lapse honesty check
edge_cases.mitigation: apply the rating-honesty check (per-review latency, later lapses) before treating a concept as mastered-easy

edge_cases.description: Mastered-easy cards are postponed night after night, accumulating a hidden backlog that lapses in a wave
edge_cases.trigger: load budgeting defers the same easy pile repeatedly without a cap
edge_cases.mitigation: cap consecutive postponements of a card and re-admit deferred easy cards before their predicted-R drops too far

edge_cases.description: Due reviews fill the day and crowd out the protected new-material acquisition quota
edge_cases.trigger: the queue lets reviews consume the whole time budget
edge_cases.mitigation: reserve the acquisition quota first and trim by postponing mastered-easy reviews, letting only the burnout guard shrink the quota

edge_cases.description: The burnout guard fires after a single frustrated session and permanently softens difficulty
edge_cases.trigger: the guard's sensitivity is set too high with no recovery path
edge_cases.mitigation: require a sustained frustration/abandonment signal to trigger and let the band drift back toward ~85% as engagement recovers

edge_cases.description: The nightly calibration step is not idempotent, so a mid-job crash and re-run produce a different target band
edge_cases.trigger: the step mutates history in place instead of being a pure function of stored actuals
edge_cases.mitigation: compute the band as a pure function of stored actuals and prior band, writing new data only, so re-runs reproduce the result

workflow.action: Establish desirable difficulties and the fluency caveat
workflow.description: Name the four desirable difficulties and state that in-session fluency is a misleading signal
workflow.gate: the four difficulties are cited FACT and fluency is stated to be judged by delayed retrieval, not session ease

workflow.action: Set the ~85% difficulty target with its exact tags
workflow.description: State the Wilson et al. 2019 result FACT and the ~85% human target ESTIMATE, and separate the acquisition and retention dials
workflow.gate: 15.87% is FACT, the ~85% human target is an ESTIMATE default not a law, and the two dials are declared separate

workflow.description: Rule out DKT/full IRT for one user and select Elo as the streaming estimator
workflow.gate: DKT is marked population-scale, IRT conceptual-only, and Elo the practical single-user estimator

workflow.description: Define p=1/(1+e^-(theta-d)), the symmetric update with K, and the invert-to-p-approx-0.85 selection
workflow.gate: the expectation, update and Rasch/1PL equivalence are stated with the FACT/ESTIMATE tags and the selection rule

workflow.action: Weight evidence by the guessing floor and prefer generation
workflow.description: Apply c approx 0.25 for 4-option MCQ, down-weight MCQ corrects vs free recall, and prefer retrieval/generation formats
workflow.gate: MCQ corrects are discounted by the guessing floor and free recall is preferred where feasible

workflow.description: Maintain per-concept RD growing with inactivity and require low RD before acting
workflow.gate: an RD-style uncertainty gates action and the exact Glicko equations are flagged UNKNOWN and not hard-coded

workflow.action: Ground interleaving and reserve blocking for first exposure
workflow.description: Cite Brunmair g=0.42 and Rohrer d=0.83, feed the confusion matrix into pairing, and block only first encounters
workflow.gate: the effect sizes are cited FACT, confused pairs drive interleaving, and blocking is limited to first encounters

workflow.action: Define the success-band controller with burnout and coasting limits
workflow.description: Select at p approx 0.85, loosen to 0.7 on coasting (>92%), tighten to 0.9 on frustration (<70% or abandonment)
workflow.gate: the controller reads guessing-floor-adjusted low-RD actuals and moves the band within the stated thresholds

workflow.action: Detect coasting and budget repetition load
workflow.description: Identify mastered-easy via low-D/high-S + theta >> d with the honesty check and postpone those cards first
workflow.gate: mastered-easy cards are postponed first (lowest predicted-R loss) and weak-concept/acquisition cards are protected

workflow.action: Assemble tomorrow's interleaved queue with a protected acquisition quota
workflow.description: Combine reviews + probes + acquisition quota, order by interleaving, select acquisition at p approx 0.85, trim to budget
workflow.gate: the queue interleaves confused pairs, hits the protected acquisition quota at p approx 0.85, and fits the time budget

workflow.action: Recalibrate nightly and compose the go/no-go verdict
workflow.description: Adjust the band idempotently from rolling actuals, score success-vs-band, and pass the four-lens verdict
workflow.gate: the band is re-tuned idempotently and the verdict conditions a go on setpoint honesty, evidence integrity, difficulty engineering and learner protection

priority_rationale: The desirable-difficulties principle, the fluency caveat, the single-user estimator scope and the ~85% setpoint come first because every controller depends on the theory, the estimator choice and the target; the acquisition-vs-retention dial separation, the Elo estimator, the guessing-floor weighting and the RD uncertainty next, because they are the metrics and guards that turn the setpoint into a trustworthy per-concept challenge estimate; the interleaving evidence, first-encounter blocking, confusion-driven interleaving and generation preference then engineer the difficulties into the practice mix; the success-band controller with coasting detection, burnout guarding, load budgeting, retention calibration and the acquisition quota form the closed loop; and the nightly calibration step, the challenge feedback loop, the queue assembly and the merged go/no-go come last because they compose every upstream output into a reproducible nightly plan and a defensible calibrate/hold verdict.

dominance_rules.rule: Delayed retrieval dominates in-session fluency as the learning signal
dominance_rules.rationale: desirable difficulties depress in-session ease, so smoothness is a misleading cue
dominance_rules.trigger: a decision is being made off how easy a session felt or a confident self-rating
dominance_rules.action: judge learning by next-day and later retrieval and treat self-rated ease as a checkable claim, not evidence

dominance_rules.rule: The ESTIMATE tag dominates any citation of the ~85% figure as a human law
dominance_rules.rationale: the result is derived from gradient-descent learning algorithms, not a human RCT
dominance_rules.trigger: the ~85% target is stated as a proven human optimum
dominance_rules.action: keep 15.87% as FACT, present ~85% as a principled ESTIMATE default, and allow per-learner divergence

dominance_rules.rule: Dial separation dominates any attempt to unify acquisition and retention targets
dominance_rules.rationale: they measure different quantities and steer different subsystems
dominance_rules.trigger: a change tries to set FSRS desired_retention to the acquisition target or vice versa
dominance_rules.action: keep the acquisition ~80-85% dial and the FSRS 0.8-0.97 dial separate, each validated against its own actuals

dominance_rules.rule: Guessing-floor-adjusted evidence dominates raw success rates
dominance_rules.rationale: an MCQ correct carries ~25% chance mass and inflates apparent mastery
dominance_rules.trigger: a success rate is computed or a rating updated from raw MCQ corrects
dominance_rules.action: discount MCQ corrects by the guessing floor and weight free recall higher before any target comparison

dominance_rules.rule: Low RD dominates responsiveness when acting on a weakness
dominance_rules.rationale: a low theta may be under-sampled noise rather than a real weakness
dominance_rules.trigger: the controller is about to remediate or change difficulty on a low estimate
dominance_rules.action: require low RD first; spend probe slots to reduce RD before acting

dominance_rules.rule: The burnout guard dominates the desirable-difficulty pull
dominance_rules.rationale: a learner who disengages learns nothing, so engagement outranks any single session's difficulty
dominance_rules.trigger: frustration, mid-session abandonment or chronically-unfinished plans appear
dominance_rules.action: force the band easier (toward 0.9), protect a win floor, and act only in the easier direction

dominance_rules.rule: The protected acquisition quota dominates load trimming
dominance_rules.rationale: new learning is the point and reviews must not crowd it out
dominance_rules.trigger: the day is over budget and trimming is needed
dominance_rules.action: postpone mastered-easy reviews first and never raid the acquisition quota; only the burnout guard may shrink it

dominance_rules.rule: First-encounter blocking dominates interleaving for a brand-new topic
dominance_rules.rationale: interleaving helps once items are confusable but clean initial encoding comes first
dominance_rules.trigger: a tag is being encountered for the very first time
dominance_rules.action: block that first encounter, then fold the tag into the interleaved daily mix

dominance_rules.rule: Idempotency dominates convenience in the nightly step
dominance_rules.rationale: a crash-and-rerun must reproduce the same band for the pipeline to be trustworthy
dominance_rules.trigger: the calibration step would mutate history in place
dominance_rules.action: compute the band as a pure function of stored actuals and write only new data

anti_rework_rules.rule: Tag the ~85% figure (15.87% FACT, ~85% human target ESTIMATE) at first use
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a later retraction when someone treats an algorithm result as a human law and builds on it

anti_rework_rules.rule: Declare the acquisition and FSRS-retention dials separate before wiring any controller
anti_rework_rules.prevents: re-plumbing after a conflated dial mis-schedules reviews or mis-sets acquisition difficulty

anti_rework_rules.rule: Down-weight MCQ corrects by the guessing floor from the first success-rate computation
anti_rework_rules.prevents: recalibrating the whole success band after discovering it was steered off guessing-inflated rates

anti_rework_rules.rule: Gate every weakness action on low RD from the outset
anti_rework_rules.prevents: remediation effort and difficulty churn spent on under-sampled noise that later self-corrects

anti_rework_rules.rule: Reserve the acquisition quota before laying out reviews in the queue
anti_rework_rules.prevents: rebuilding the day after reviews crowd out new learning

anti_rework_rules.rule: Wire the burnout guard as easier-only before tuning challenge upward
anti_rework_rules.prevents: having to unwind an over-aggressive difficulty push that drove abandonment

anti_rework_rules.rule: Restrict blocking to first encounters when the queue-ordering rule is first written
anti_rework_rules.prevents: re-sequencing after blocking is found to persist past initial encoding

anti_rework_rules.rule: Make the nightly calibration step idempotent (write-only) when it is first built
anti_rework_rules.prevents: debugging non-reproducible bands after a mid-job crash corrupts the tuning

iteration_protocol.trigger: a human RCT or per-learner tuning quantifies an optimal acquisition success rate different from ~85%
iteration_protocol.action: update the setpoint and the success-band center, re-tag the evidence, and re-check the controller thresholds

iteration_protocol.trigger: the success band oscillates or chases noise off short windows
iteration_protocol.action: lengthen the rolling window, add hysteresis to the >92%/<70% thresholds, and re-validate the nightly step

iteration_protocol.trigger: later lapses spike on concepts marked coasting, showing the rating-honesty check missed decay
iteration_protocol.action: tighten the latency/later-lapse honesty check and re-admit wrongly-shed cards before their predicted-R drops

iteration_protocol.trigger: the canonical Glicko spec becomes fetchable so the RD equations can be verified
iteration_protocol.action: replace the RD-style approximation with the verified update and re-tune the confidence threshold

iteration_protocol.trigger: a newer interleaving meta-analysis or domain-specific (math) evidence revises the effect
iteration_protocol.action: update the interleaving policy and the first-encounter blocking window

iteration_protocol.trigger: AI free-recall grading accuracy changes materially
iteration_protocol.action: re-weight free-recall vs MCQ evidence and re-set the format preference

iteration_protocol.trigger: the burnout guard fires too often (over-easy) or too rarely (burnout slips through)
iteration_protocol.action: re-tune the frustration/abandonment sensitivity and the recovery-toward-85% drift

iteration_protocol.trigger: multi-learner data appears making population calibration feasible
iteration_protocol.action: revisit the single-user estimator choice and whether a richer model now applies
